 Google Vids Gets 15-Second AI Video Gen Free With Omni Flash
 Articles Newsletters Articles Newsletters AI video generation 11/5/2026 Google Vids Gets 15-Second AI Video Gen Free With Omni Flash
 Google rolls out Omni 1.2 Flash model to Vids, tripling video length to 15 seconds
 By The Tech Buzz Add as a preferred source on Google Google Vids interface displayed on a laptop screen with AI video generation controls and preview visible. AI-generated illustration by The Tech Buzz. Edited by Barnabas Oretan (The Tech Buzz). AI-generated image Listen to this article 5 min listen 1 x 00:00 05:00 Google just turbocharged its Workspace video tool with a serious AI upgrade. The company rolled out Omni 1.2 Flash to Google Vids today, letting users generate 15-second AI video clips at no cost—triple the previous 5-second limit. The move puts Google squarely in competition with standalone AI video generators while keeping the capability free for Workspace users, a strategic play that could reshape how businesses approach video content creation.
 Google is making a calculated bet that the future of AI video generation lives inside productivity suites, not standalone apps. The company announced today that Google Vids —its Workspace video creation tool—now runs on Omni 1.2 Flash, the latest iteration of its multimodal AI model that can generate 15-second video clips from text prompts.
 The upgrade matters because it's free. While competitors like Runway and Pika charge subscription fees for similar capabilities, Google is bundling longer-form AI video generation directly into Workspace at no extra cost. According to the company's announcement , users can now create clips three times longer than the previous 5-second limit, with noticeably better scene consistency and visual coherence.
 Advertisement
 The timing aligns with Google's broader push to slash Gemini video pricing by 30% , a move announced earlier this week that signaled the company's intent to undercut rivals on AI infrastructure costs. Omni 1.2 Flash represents the consumer-facing counterpart to that enterprise strategy—make the tech accessible enough that it becomes the default choice before users even consider alternatives.
 What sets this release apart is the integration angle. Google Vids already sits inside the Workspace ecosystem alongside Docs, Sheets, and Slides, which means 3+ billion active users have instant access without downloading new software or managing separate subscriptions. The 15-second generation window is long enough for social media clips, product demos, or presentation B-roll—the exact use cases where businesses currently outsource to freelancers or struggle with complex editing software.
 The technical improvements in Omni 1.2 Flash focus on temporal consistency, the perpetual challenge in AI video where objects morph or scenes shift unnaturally between frames. Google claims the new model maintains better visual coherence across the full 15-second duration, though the company hasn't released benchmarks comparing it to competitors like OpenAI's Sora or Meta's Movie Gen.
 Advertisement
 This launch also comes as Google faces mounting pressure to monetize its $200 billion AI investments amid slowing search revenue growth. By embedding advanced generative AI into Workspace, the company creates a defensive moat around its productivity suite while potentially justifying future price increases for premium tiers.
 The competitive implications ripple beyond just video tools. Microsoft has been aggressively integrating AI into Office 365 through Copilot, charging $30 per user monthly for advanced features. Google's decision to keep Omni 1.2 Flash free in Vids puts pressure on Microsoft to match or risk losing ground in the enterprise productivity wars.
 For creators and marketers, the practical value hinges on output quality. Fifteen seconds is enough for Instagram Reels, TikTok clips, or LinkedIn video posts, but only if the results look professional enough to skip manual editing. Early tests will determine whether Omni 1.2 Flash can truly replace human-created content or if it remains a rough-draft tool that still requires significant post-production.
 Advertisement
 The free tier strategy also raises questions about Google's long-term monetization plan. Giving away advanced AI video generation at scale isn't cheap—training and inference costs for multimodal models run into millions of dollars monthly. Either Google plans to introduce premium Vids features later, or it's treating video generation as a loss leader to lock users deeper into the Workspace ecosystem.
 What's clear is that Google is racing to make AI video generation feel as mundane as spell-check. By the time competitors figure out pricing and distribution, Google wants 15-second AI clips to already be the default way millions of people create video content at work.
 Google's Omni 1.2 Flash rollout in Vids represents a strategic shift toward embedded AI rather than standalone tools. By offering 15-second video generation free inside Workspace, the company is betting that convenience and integration will beat feature-rich paid alternatives. The real test comes in the next quarter when usage data reveals whether businesses actually adopt AI video at scale or if this remains a novelty feature. For now, Google has put every competitor on notice that the AI video wars won't be won on quality alone—distribution and pricing matter just as much.

 What is Google Vids and how does it work? 
 Google Vids is a free AI video creation tool built into Google Workspace that generates video clips from text prompts. The latest Omni 1.2 Flash model creates 15-second videos with improved scene consistency. It's available to all 3+ billion Workspace users at no additional cost. How long can Google Vids generate videos with Omni 1.2 Flash? 
 Google Vids now generates 15-second AI video clips using Omni 1.2 Flash, triple the previous 5-second limit. This length is sufficient for social media clips, product demos, and presentation B-roll without additional editing. Does Google Vids cost money to use? 
 No, Google Vids is completely free for all Google Workspace users. The 15-second AI video generation with Omni 1.2 Flash requires no additional subscription or cost, unlike competitors like Runway and Pika that charge subscription fees. How does Google Vids compare to other AI video generators? 
 Google Vids is free and integrated into Workspace, while competitors like Runway and Pika charge subscriptions. Google Vids offers 15-second generation with improved scene consistency. Its main advantage is accessibility to 3+ billion Workspace users without separate software downloads. What improvements does Omni 1.2 Flash bring to Google Vids? 
 Omni 1.2 Flash extends video generation from 5 to 15 seconds and improves temporal consistency—preventing objects from morphing or scenes shifting unnaturally between frames. The model maintains better visual coherence throughout the full video duration. When did Google Vids get the Omni 1.2 Flash update? 
 Google announced the Omni 1.2 Flash rollout to Google Vids today, making 15-second AI video generation available immediately to all Workspace users. The update represents Google's latest move in competitive AI video generation pricing. More in AI
